stories.h: Boeing layoff notices due Dec. 9, union still in dark
stories.s: Boeing plans to cut 5% of its commercial airplane workforce. SPEEA says some employees will get 60-day notices Dec. 9, with layoffs effective Feb. 12, but managers couldn't say who or how many.

stories.h: Seattle and most WA cities raise property taxes again
stories.s: Seattle's council is expected to approve its routine 1% levy increase, the most allowed under I-747; Bellevue, Tacoma, Everett, Kent and others are doing the same. Falling office values shift more burden to homeowners.

stories.h: Olympia clears 'The Jungle,' its largest homeless encampment
stories.s: Crews are clearing the 20-acre camp off Martin Way East, home to nearly 300 people; 40 have been temporarily housed so far. The city will ask lawmakers for $6.5 million for shelter units.

stories.h: State parks commission rejects golf course at Westport Light
stories.s: Commissioners voted down a proposed 18-hole links course at the coastal state park, citing wetland impacts, Quinault Nation fish-habitat concerns, doubts about the developer and the state's budget shortfall.

talking.h: Catton's first NHL hat trick powers Kraken past Canucks
talking.s: Berkly Catton scored three times as Seattle beat Vancouver 5-1 Thursday, ending a three-game skid. The Kraken's 24-5 first-period shot edge set a franchise record.

talking.h: Seattle Christmas Market opens today at Seattle Center
talking.s: The European-style holiday village begins its fourth season Nov. 20 and runs through Dec. 26, with vendors, mulled wine, a carousel and Santa photos. Tickets start at $6.99.

talking.h: Bellevue homeowner shot at bear in Lakemont yard
talking.s: A homeowner near Cougar Mountain reportedly hit a bear on Nov. 8; WDFW never found the animal. Neighbors say a mother bear and two cubs haven't been seen since.

coming.h: Razor clam digs open Thanksgiving week
coming.s: WDFW approved five evening digs, Nov. 24–28, at Mocrocks and Copalis only; Long Beach and Twin Harbors stay closed over marine toxins. Diggers 16+ need a 2026-27 license.

coming.h: Thanksgiving travel crunch on highways and ferries
coming.s: WSDOT's travel charts cover Nov. 25–29 for I-5, I-90 and US 2. Ferries will be busiest westbound Nov. 25–26 and eastbound Nov. 28–29; reservations urged.
